name: Waris Ahmad Faizi
title: Ph.D. Student in Sociology
tagline: Economic Sociology · Digital Sociology · Work, Labor, and Organizations · Computational Social Science
bio: I am a Ph.D. student in the Department of Sociology at Virginia Tech, where I study economic sociology, digital sociology, and the sociology of work, labor, and organizations. My research asks how economic value is produced, measured, and unequally distributed — across labor markets, platform and influencer economies, and the moral evaluation of care work.

Methodologically, I work at the intersection of quantitative methods and computational social science. I use large-scale survey data, computational text analysis, and systematic review to study occupational change and reskilling in the age of AI, economic precarity and the quality of work life, social capital and economic mobility.

Before joining Virginia Tech, I earned an M.A. in Sociology from the American University of Central Asia, an M.A. in Economics from the OSCE Academy, and a B.A. in Economics from Kabul University. I was a visiting graduate student at the University of Tübingen (Erasmus+ and DAAD) and an exchange student at Otto-von-Guericke University Magdeburg (Erasmus+). I have also worked as a university lecturer and researcher, including as a Research Fellow with the Central Asia Program at George Washington University, an intern at the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) Secretariat, and a research consultant on a World Bank project.

In 2026, I was a fellow at the Summer Institute in Computational Social Science (SICSS) at Stanford University and a teaching assistant for the ICPSR Summer Program in Quantitative Methods at the University of Michigan.
